correctness.rationale: For each odd q the map from six symmetric structure constants to four homogeneous cubic coefficients is onto with q^2 radial fibers. Nonzero idempotents are exactly rational eigenline roots with nonzero eigenvalue. Two independent square-zero vectors force rank at most one, so perfect idempotent-free tensors have at most one rational root. The irreducible-cubic, linear-times-irreducible-quadratic, and triple-root cubic counts are exact; the first has q^2 perfect lifts, the second q, and the third q−1 after subtracting its unique rank-one lift. Zero cubic yields only radial multiplication and cannot be perfect and idempotent-free. Summing gives the stated all-q formula, checked separately at q=3 and q=5 by enumeration of all q^6 tables. Finite checks alone do not prove general q.

value.rationale: The exact number and three projective-factorization strata classify the naturally motivated rational-idempotent-free locus within every rank-two symmetric binary algebra over odd finite fields, a complete quantitative invariant not given by individual-algebra idempotent algorithms or unfiltered isomorphism-class enumerations. Its limiting density 1/3 distinguishes rational arithmetic from algebraically closed idempotent behavior and identifies two square-zero degeneration contributions. This is a substantive finite-field count with a structural explanation, not a single arbitrary numerical slice.
